front.zh: 現代俳句 & 變奏   系列《6》

en: The dream's expanse is vast, fit only for wandering
Dwelling wherever water and grass are found
With you
The green mountains remain as before
How many times the sunset has reddened
Better to go home -- but how can I go home?

points.zh:
滾滾長江東逝水，浪花淘盡英雄。
是非成敗轉頭空。
青山依舊在，幾度夕陽紅。
白髮漁樵江渚上，慣看秋月春風。
一壼濁酒喜相逢。
古今多少事，都付笑談中。
--明。楊慎《臨江仙》
points.en:
The rolling waters of the Yangtze flow ever eastward, its waves washing away all heroes.
Right and wrong, success and failure, all turn to nothing in a single glance back.
The green mountains remain as before, through however many crimson sunsets.
White-haired fishermen and woodcutters on the river's sandbanks, long used to the autumn moon and spring breeze.
A jug of turbid wine, a joyful meeting; the affairs of past and present, all given over to laughter and talk.
-- Ming dynasty. Yang Shen, 'Linjiangxian'

en: A journey of color and beauty
Bit by bit, half-hidden, half-revealed
A life as plain as vegetables and tofu
You turn and leave, like mist
Moonlight arrives at the window
Days return to the original loneliness
Projecting the fullness of the rice ears
Trampling the setting sun's gold to fragments
Impressions of home: a water buffalo

points.zh:
一行一行笨拙的足印
沿着寬厚的田畝
也沿着祖先
滴不盡的汗漬
寫上誠誠懇懇的土地
不爭、不吵、沈默的等待
--吳晟。詩《 吾鄉印象 : 土  》
points.en:
Row after row of clumsy footprints
along the broad, generous fields
also along the ancestors'
never-ending trickle of sweat
inscribed upon the earnest, honest land
not contending, not quarreling, waiting in silence
-- Wu Sheng, from the poem "Impressions of My Hometown: Soil"

en: Dusk, walking with you
Soft in tone
Speaking of misty waters and things gone by
Emptiness -- a bird flies into the deep mountains
Stillness—the moon imprinted on the cold pool
Zen -- the person at leisure, osmanthus blossoms falling

points.zh:
人閑桂花落，夜靜春山空。
月出驚山鳥，時鳴春澗中。
--唐。王維《鳥鳴澗》

en: Wrinkles like flowing water
There is a story hidden away
Let it hide
Having walked through
A log bridge that follows its own will
Looking back again, the world of dust already lies between
The arc of the swing, back and forth
Setting off ripples, rippling on ~~~~
Cannot hold back the setting sun on the silvergrass

points.zh:
2017 諾貝爾物理獎得獎者是 85 歲的萊納 · 魏斯（Rainer Weiss）、77 歲的基普 · 索恩（ Kip Thorn）、81 歲的巴瑞 · 巴利許 （Barry Barish），他們因為 LIGO（雷射干涉重力波天文台， Laser Interferometer Gravitational-Wave Observatory 的縮寫）探測器及重力波 ( Gravitational Waves ) 探測的成就而獲獎。   愛因斯坦在 1916年發表廣義相對論時，就提出了重力波理論 : 重力為時空發生彎曲的結果，宇宙中發生天體活動（黑洞互撞、中子星互撞等）時，會引起從源頭向外以光速傳播的波動現象，產生時空的「漣漪」。重力波能夠穿透電磁波所無法穿透的空間，過去科學家推測，重力波能夠幫助了解位於宇宙遠處的各種天體，例如黑洞，這類天體無法用光學望遠鏡和電子望遠鏡等傳統方式用「看的」觀測，但可能用重力波來達成（有點像用「聽」的）。然而重力波相對於電磁波等基本波動而言非常微弱，困擾了無數的科學家，甚至 愛因斯坦本人都不抱太大希望，一直要到 100 年後的 2016 年科學家們才終於突破，藉由LIGO測到了重力波。學界普遍認為，重力波的發現是物理學和天文學的一項重大突破，稱之爲『物理界聖杯』。它開啟了人類探索宇宙的一扇大門，甚至可能揭開暗物質和宇宙形成等的奧秘。今年十月首次測得中子星互撞的重力波，帶動探知地球重金屬如金、白金、鈾等的來源。
在秘魯「馬丘比丘」古城内的金字塔形的最高建築上，有一個全世界僅存，具極高度智慧象徵的「栓日石」( Intihuatana )。此乃印加人依據太陽周年運行軌道所設計的「日晷」。考古學家認為這是馬丘比丘最神聖的建築。栓日石是一塊高約二米的長方形大石盤，上有直線刻度。石盤中心有一突出石桩，隨太陽運行，石桩會在刻度上投下隂影，精確地指明一天的時間。并用栓日石來計算夏至和冬至的時令點。印加人深信「太陽神」是他們的祖先，他們是太陽之子。在每年冬至的太陽節時，卽日照最短，太陽距離最遠的一日，在此舉行祭典，祈求萬能之神將太陽栓在這塊聖石上，讓它回歸，不再遠去。
points.en:
The winners of the 2017 Nobel Prize in Physics were Rainer Weiss, 85; Kip Thorne, 77; and Barry Barish, 81. They were honored for their contributions to the LIGO (Laser Interferometer Gravitational-Wave Observatory) detector and the detection of gravitational waves. When Einstein published his general theory of relativity in 1916, he had already proposed the theory of gravitational waves: gravity results from the curvature of spacetime, and when cosmic events occur in the universe -- such as the collision of black holes or neutron stars -- they generate waves that propagate outward from the source at the speed of light, producing "ripples" in spacetime. Gravitational waves can pass through regions of space that electromagnetic waves cannot penetrate; scientists had long speculated that gravitational waves could help reveal distant celestial objects such as black holes, which cannot be observed through conventional means like optical or electronic telescopes, but might be detected through gravitational waves instead (somewhat like "listening" rather than "seeing"). However, compared to electromagnetic and other fundamental waves, gravitational waves are extremely faint, which confounded countless scientists -- even Einstein himself held little hope of their detection. It was not until 100 years later, in 2016, that scientists finally achieved a breakthrough, detecting gravitational waves through LIGO. The scientific community widely regards the discovery of gravitational waves as a major breakthrough in physics and astronomy, calling it the "holy grail of physics." It has opened a door for humanity to explore the universe, and may even help uncover the mysteries of dark matter and the origin of the cosmos. In October of that year, gravitational waves from a neutron star collision were detected for the first time, advancing understanding of the origins of heavy elements on Earth such as gold, platinum, and uranium.
At the top of the pyramid-shaped highest structure within the ancient city of Machu Picchu in Peru stands the Intihuatana stone, a uniquely surviving symbol of the high level of intelligence achieved by its builders. It is a sundial designed by the Inca based on the sun's annual orbital path. Archaeologists consider it the most sacred structure in Machu Picchu. The Intihuatana is a large rectangular stone slab roughly two meters high, marked with straight-line gradations. At its center rises a protruding stone post; as the sun moves, the post casts a shadow across the markings, precisely indicating the time of day. The stone was also used to calculate the timing of the summer and winter solstices. The Inca firmly believed that the Sun God was their ancestor, and that they themselves were children of the sun. Each year at the winter solstice festival -- the day with the shortest sunlight and the sun at its farthest distance -- they held ceremonies here to pray to the all-powerful god to tether the sun to this sacred stone, so that it would return and not depart forever.
